I'm looking at the coordinates of the ligand L1102 atoms and now checking which nearby protein residues, possibly around positions 24, 25, 28, and 31, could be in contact with it.

Checking distances, ARG24 sidechain atoms (CD, NE) and backbone O come within ~3-4 angstroms of the ligand's O1 and C1 atoms, suggesting a direct interaction. I'm now checking whether GLU31 or LEU25 also fall within this range, but their coordinates place them much farther away.

LYS28's NZ terminus lands about 3.46 angstroms from C2, qualifying it as another nearby residue, though its other sidechain carbons like CD and CE fall just outside the 4 angstrom cutoff. I'm also confirming ARG24's remaining atoms are fine and ruling out GLU22 and LEU21 as too distant in the z-coordinate.

GLU27's CB atom comes in right at 3.88 angstroms from O1, so that residue qualifies too.

Its CA and CG are too far though. I'm now ruling out several other residues -- LYS23, SER26, GLU31, LEU25, and the backbone N of residue 28 -- all sitting too far from the target atoms. I'm also checking whether anything sits near the C5/C6/O6 region around z -10 to -11, but LYS38, CYS42, and GLU31's OE2 all come up too distant. So it looks like the qualifying residues so far are ARG24, LYS28, and GLU27, and I'm double-checking GLU20 and ARG24's CB atom to make sure nothing else slips in.

ARG24's carbonyl carbon checks out at 3.79 Å. Other nearby residues like LYS28 and GLU31 come back too far, so the final contacts settle on A:R24, A:E27, and A:K28. Let me just double check there's nothing else nearby I'm missing.
